Good morning, readers! Grab your tea and catch up with today's big headlines from politics, national and global events, sports, and entertainment.
Delhi woke up to Diwali on Sunday after recording its most polluted festival eve in a decade. The city's air quality index (AQI) stood at 369 at 4 pm on Saturday, placing it in the ‘very poor’ category on the Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) 0-500 scale. This was the highest AQI recorded on the day before Diwali since 2016, when it touched 404. Read the full story here .
The embassy of India in Tehran celebrated Diwali with members of the Indian and Iranian communities, along with diplomats, bringing together people to mark the festival of lights and experience the country’s rich cultural traditions. The celebrations featured the lighting of ceremonial lamps by the ambassador, along with music, fireworks and festive treats. The embassy said celebrating Diwali in Iran was a reminder of how traditions transcend borders and strengthen India-Iran ties. Read the full story here .
Israel's president on Saturday chose Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's strongest rival, to try to form a new government, Israeli media reported, following a deadlocked election that left neither man with a clear path to power. Read the full story here .
Punjab Police has secured the return of wanted gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi from Ethiopia in a major operation. Gurwinder arrived at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport in the early hours on Sunday. He is being taken to Punjab by a team of the Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF). Read the full story here .
Diljit Dosanjh 's upcoming concert in Indore has run into fresh trouble, with the district's child protection authorities asking organisers to keep four of his songs out of the setlist. The singer is scheduled to perform in the city on November 15 as part of his Aura India Tour, but a notice issued ahead of the show has put restrictions on some of his popular tracks over concerns about their lyrics and the impact they could have on children. Read the full story here .
East Bengal FC scripted history by becoming the first Indian club to qualify for the knockout stages of the AFC Women's Champions League despite a 0-2 defeat to 4.25 SC of DPR Korea in their final Group B match of the 2026-27 group stage at the Kishore Bharati Krirangan in Kolkata on Saturday. Stories undergo editorial scrutiny and verification processes to ensure accuracy, fairness and relevance, and are updated as events evolve and additional information becomes available. Whether covering a key political decision in New Delhi, an economic policy shift affecting millions, a landmark court ruling or a major global event, the HT News Desk aims to provide readers with reliable, fact-based journalism that delivers not only the latest developments but also the context and analysis needed to understand their wider implications.
